Got it for $24, and that included both Season Passes and the base game. It's been well worth that price.

I'm always a little sketchy on Warhammer games because it feels like they're either dog-shit or ok/goodish —there's never much in-between.

This one, however, was actually really good. Graphically it's very nice, and the single-player story was also pretty good, even for a newer Warhammer fan like me who's still learning the lore.

The gameplay, though? That's where it's at.

The melee and gunplay are phenomenal. The gore, the impact, and the sheer brutality of it all feel like an early 2000s game and hit that adrenaline spike that keeps you wanting to play.

I'd give it an 8.5/10 at minimum. Some days it honestly feels even better than that.

The one flaw that drags the score down is the grind. For a new player, getting even a single class to a workable state for Operations, Multiplayer, or Siege is about 100 hours of grinding. They really need to increase the XP gains, especially now that the game has been out for a while. On top of that, weekends should give an even bigger XP boost to help newer players catch up

love this game. it is a great sequel to the original. Most the combat does a great job of making you feel like a space marine, where so many previous ones have failed to grasp that fantasy.
Only real complaints I have are is the difficulty can be a little high for some fans of the IP who are not great at twitch/skill games, as it relies heavily on parries. They seemed to have borrowed from Souls-Like games for the their "duels" with bigger enemies where you have to time your blocks and know when to commit to an attack. However, there is a reason most of those games only send a couple enemies at you at once. In this game you have the world war z / left for dead swarm mechanics happening at the same time. This can be a bit tough to get used to handling.
10/10 the Emperor Protects
Just play darktide. You feel more like a space marine in that game than you do this one.

Let me be clear, Space Marine 2 can be a good game! But it's not what it was advertised as. I expected a long singleplayer campaign that made me really experience the whole of the Tyrannid faction in Warhammer 40K. Instead I got a few bugs (of the Tyrannid variety), a few more chaos marines, and a story so short I've had visits to the bathroom that have felt longer. Meanwhile the multiplayer game modes seem to get all the attention.

If you want to be a space marine, then sure, this is the game for you... So long as you don't want a good story, and just want to shoot other players. If you want a good story, and the ability to be a space marine, go play the first game. And if you want good mulitplayer shooter action go play any other popular multiplayer shooter. Marvel Rivals is free to play, and doesn't take up as much space as this game does.

I think a lot of popularity of this game comes from people who love the 40K universe, and that's perfectly fine, it's a great story universe! But this game is not the pinnicle of what can been done in this universe. It's not even the best product of what HAS been done in this universe. Go play Darktide, or Vermintide I don't know about Darktide, but Vermintide is 10X better.

Great gameplay and graphics — I genuinely give them high praise.
However, I was really disappointed to find that the outfits I had previously unlocked were taken away after the update. Sometimes, the motivation to keep playing comes from earning a specific skill, piece of gear, or cosmetic outfit. When those rewards are taken back and I’m forced to unlock them all over again, it honestly kills the drive to keep going.

Also:

1.Connection quality still needs improvement.

2.There are too few co-op PvE stages.

3.After unlocking Transcendent Mastery, I had to re-unlock other skills again — which felt unnecessary.

Some players might find this kind of reset refreshing, but for me, it was more frustrating than fun.

This game astounded me with how good it actually is. I played Space Marine 1 years ago and the jump in quality here is insane. The story mode itself is not bad but what really shines is the PvE content. I found myself having an extreme amount of fun picking up new classes and seeing how they function. I can see myself playing this for a while longer while Space Marine 3 is cooking in the background.

I normally hate PvP in games like this, but after playing some matches its not a terrible distraction if you're actually curious in trying it out. However, the new ordeals they added that forces you to get 500 melee kills and 500 ranged kills is a bit much for sure. The new cosmetics should have been tied to PvE imo, but we'll see if Saber changes their minds on that one.

Overall, I can highly recommend this game especially if you get it on sale. A lot of fun to be had and I can't wait to see what the new class brings to the game once it releases.
